description: AGP has a minimum required Gradle version that climbs independently of AGP's own version number. Grouped with the wrapper so a bump never lands AGP ahead of a Gradle it needs. Grouping only combines updates that are due at the same time — the minimumReleaseAge override below is what keeps Gradle from being the thing an AGP bump waits on.
Gradle releases are stable on arrival, so the wrapper skips the default minimumReleaseAge and is essentially always at Gradle's latest.

KSP's version is only valid for one specific Kotlin version, and the Compose compiler plugin must match the Kotlin version exactly. Grouped so a bump proposes all three in one PR instead of breaking the build.
All androidx.room artifacts are released together and must be on the same version — Google requires this explicitly.
CameraX recommends keeping camera-core/camera2/lifecycle/view on the same version.

activity-compose 1.13.0 breaks `./gradlew lintDebug` with a dependency resolution conflict (androidx.concurrent:concurrent-futures strict-version mismatch via androidx.test). `recreateWhen: never` is needed because the `recreateWhen: always` above would otherwise reopen a closed PR from its still-existing branch even with `enabled: false`. Re-enable once a version resolves cleanly against the pinned androidx.test artifacts.

Maven 3.10.0 changed how it lays out the staged bundle central-publishing-maven-plugin zips up for Maven Central, which that plugin's bundle validator now rejects ('Bundle has content that does NOT have a .pom file'). Reported upstream at mavenplugins/central-publishing-maven-plugin#78. Raise this ceiling once a Maven/plugin release fixes the interaction.
